text: 2,3/   a. Read the passage and answer the following questions: S$03,7 The choices we make on a daily basis—wearing a seatbelt, lifting heavy objects correctly or purposely staying out of any dangerous situation—can either ensure our safety or bring about potentially harmful circumstances. You and I need to make a decision that we are going to get our lives in order. Exercising self-control, self-discipline and establishing boundaries and borders in our lives are some of the most important things we can do. A life without discipline is one that’s filled with carelessness. We can think it’s kind of exciting to live life on the edge. We like the image of “Yeah! That’s me! Living on the edge! Woo-hoo!” It’s become a popular way to look at life. But if you see, even highways have lines, which provide margins for our safety while we’re driving. If we go over one'side, we'll go into the ditch. If we cross over the line in the middle, we could get killed. And we like those lines because they help to keep us safe. Sometimes we don’t even realize how lines help to keep us safe. I’m not proud of this, but for the first 20 years of my life at work, I ignored my limits. I felt horrible, physically, most of the time. I used to tell myself “I know I have limits and that I’ve reached them, but I’m going to ignore them and see if or how long I can get by with it.” I ran to doctors, trying to make myself feel better through pills, vitamins, natural stuff and anything could get my hands on. Some of the doctors would tell me, “It’s just stress.” That just made me mad.   thought stress meant you don’t like what you do or can’t handle life, and I love what I do. But I kept pushing myself traveling, doing speaking engagements and so on— simply exhausting myself. Finally, I understood I was living an unsustainable life and needed to make some changes in my outlook and lifestyle. You and   don’t have to be like everyone else or keep up with anyone else. Each of us needs to be exactly the way we are, and we don’t have to apologize for it. We’re not all alike and we need to find a comfort zone in which we can enjoy our lives instead of making ourselves sick with an overload of stress and pressure.

text: 2,3 Create a precis (60 words) of the following passage and include a title for the same. Almost every organism has the tendency to react to certain stimuli for survival. This reaction to each and every situation has an evolutionary basis of adaptation. The study of human emotions dates back to the 19th century and psychologists have since then discovered many reasons for every emotion, yet these are just theories. The arousal of emotions and their assumed structures is said to occur due to repeated encounters with a situation foilowed by the adaptation of the encounter. Human emotions have been linked to adaptively regulate emotion-gathering mechanisms. The emotion of fear which is associated with ancient parts of the brain has presumably evolved among our pre-mammal ancestors while the emotion of a mother’s love called the ‘filial emotion’ has seen to evolve among early mammals. Various emotions work as manipulative strategies that favours survival. Feigning emotions by an accused person may help him be saved from the punishment. An exaggerated display of anger is also associated with manipulating or threatening someone. Despite there being several emotions for various events, ironically the most interesting emotion is the emotion of disgust. Disgust is aroused when the body senses a danger to the immunity or the physiology of the human. The disgusted memory is associated with alerting the brain of a potentially dangerous substance. A few studies have shown that the encoding triggered in adaptive memory for problems is stronger than any other behaviour. This makes us instantly have a disgusted expression at the sight of something that makes us uncomfortable or uneasy. These expressions are also closely linked to self-protective communication. Address it to Ms Sagarika Nair of Infosys who is the head of Human Resource. %4 06 2   (i) State the principles of crafting an effective paragraph and using these principles write a paragraph which begins with: “Inside the four walls of a classroom” 3   (ii)   Read the passage below and answer the questions given We live in a world surrounded by advertisements — hoardings newspaper ads, leaflets, digital media, social media, OTT platforms,.television, radio — wherever you look, you find ads of one kind or the other. Some ads invite you to buy products or hire particular services. Some ads have a social message. Some commercials make no sense, and some make more sense than others. Most of the time, ads with a social message capture public attention and imagination. One interesting trend is that commercial ads bring in social messages — some loud and clear and some subtle. This achieves goodwill and visibility for the brand. One such example is Anouk’s Bold is Beautiful ad. The ad showcases Radhika Apte, the protagonist, calling out this silent experience of pregnant women at the workplace. Her boss, a lady, compliments Radhika, an architect, for a brilliant presentation. As they get into their car, the boss goes on to compliment Radhika’s jacket, saying that ‘it almost hides the bump.’ At this, the protagonist responds by taking on the line head on, asking why the ‘bump’ was an embarrassment. And she goes on to point out how she has been bypassed for a promotion and a male colleague preferred instead of her. She states clearly that she had been working nights and days on the project, only to be left out of an opportunity because of a completely different reason — her pregnancy. The boss tries to justify this action by deflecting responsibility, calling it a ‘management decision.’ During this conversation, the last part of the ad takes a twist. Radhika asks the driver to take a turn into a different direction. Seeing her boss’s question mark face she breaks the news that she is starting up independently, and resigning from her position. Nowhere does the ad show any product description, yet the fashion statement is clear. Anouk has garnered several followers for this kind of messaging. Questions: 1. What is the profession of the protagonist? What compliment does her boss give, that forces Radhika to question her boss? 2. Do you think this experience is specific to architects?
